children: Germany plans to tighten its takeover rules to curb so-called low-ball offers, according to a draft law seen by Reuters on Tuesday.
The finance ministry's draft would require bidders to make a new offer to the remaining shareholders at several ownership levels, not just one.
Under the current law, an acquirer must make a mandatory offer once it reaches 30% of a company's voting rights.
The draft law adds further thresholds at 35%, 40%, 45% and 50%.

The aim is to stop what government sources call "creeping in", in which a bidder makes a low voluntary offer at the legal minimum price, then builds its stake step by step without making shareholders another offer.
